title: Tie-dye, adire and even dyeing, tested and labelled

say: Tie-dye, adire and even dyeing, tested and labelled.
This is the video for module four of Advanced Home Décor and Upcycling.
Colour on cloth is at the heart of Nigerian décor, from kampala tie-dye to Yoruba adire. Both work by resist: where fabric is tightly tied, less dye reaches it.

say: You will learn tie-dye, the three adire methods, even dyeing of larger textiles, and how to test and label your work.

say: Fibre-reactive dyes bond with cotton, linen and rayon, but not polyester. For example, Ifeoma in Onitsha dyes six white 100% cotton T-shirts. She washes them first, to remove factory finishes.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's six spiral T-shirts
items: Pre-wash 100% cotton in hot water
Soak: 1 cup soda ash in about 3.8 litres
Twist a spiral, tie into 6 sections
Dye: about 2 teaspoons per cup of water
Wrap in nylon; batch 24 hours warm

say: She dissolves 1 cup of soda ash in about 3.8 litres of warm water and soaks the shirts for 20 minutes. Soda ash lets the dye bond.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's six spiral T-shirts
items: Pre-wash 100% cotton in hot water
Soak: 1 cup soda ash in about 3.8 litres
Twist a spiral, tie into 6 sections
Dye: about 2 teaspoons per cup of water
Wrap in nylon; batch 24 hours warm

say: She twists each shirt into a spiral, ties 6 sections, and squeezes on green and gold dye, each about 2 teaspoons per cup of water.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's six spiral T-shirts
items: Pre-wash 100% cotton in hot water
Soak: 1 cup soda ash in about 3.8 litres
Twist a spiral, tie into 6 sections
Dye: about 2 teaspoons per cup of water
Wrap in nylon; batch 24 hours warm

say: She wraps each shirt in nylon and leaves it warm for 24 hours. The soak and the wait make the colour permanent.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's six spiral T-shirts
items: Pre-wash 100% cotton in hot water
Soak: 1 cup soda ash in about 3.8 litres
Twist a spiral, tie into 6 sections
Dye: about 2 teaspoons per cup of water
Wrap in nylon; batch 24 hours warm

say: Then she rinses in cold water, ties still on, until the water runs nearly clear. Only then does she untie and wash hot, so loose dye cannot spread into the white areas.

panel.rule: Rinse cold with the ties on, then wash hot.

say: Adire is Yoruba indigo resist cloth, rooted in Abeokuta, Ibadan and Osogbo. Oniko ties seeds or pebbles into the cloth. Alabere sews lines of running stitch, then pulls them tight.

panel.heading: Three resist methods
left: Gives fine lines and leaf shapes
right: Dry a full day before dyeing

say: Eleko paints a thick cassava starch paste onto the cloth, or spreads it through a stencil, then dries it fully. When you use traditional motifs, credit the tradition, or better, design your own.

panel.heading: Three resist methods
left: Gives fine lines and leaf shapes
right: Dry a full day before dyeing

say: Indigo colours in the air, not in the bath. For example, Yewande in Abeokuta wets her stitched runner and dips it for about a minute. It comes out yellow-green.

panel.heading: Green in the vat, blue in the air
items: Wet tied or stitched cloth first
Dip gently; it comes out greenish
Air it until it turns blue
Dip again for a deeper blue

say: Within minutes in the air it turns blue. She repeats for 4 dips in total. One dip gives pale blue, and several give adire's deep blue.

say: Vat chemicals are dangerous. Caustic soda causes severe burns. Wear goggles, rubber gloves and long sleeves, work outdoors, and add chemicals to water slowly. A beginner can start with a ready-made kit, or work alongside an experienced dyer.

panel.rule: Caustic soda INTO water, never water onto caustic soda.

say: A blotchy curtain is hard to sell. First check the fibre. In a careful burn test outdoors, cotton smells like burning paper and polyester melts into a hard bead.

panel.heading: Nneka dyes four cushion covers
items: Check it is cotton, not polyester
Weigh dry: 800 g
Water 20:1: 16 litres
Pre-wet, dissolve fully, stir often

say: Then work by weight. For example, Nneka in Owerri has four cushion covers weighing 800 g dry. For a medium shade she uses 2%, which is 16 g of dye.

panel.heading: Nneka dyes four cushion covers
items: Check it is cotton, not polyester
Weigh dry: 800 g
Water 20:1: 16 litres
Pre-wet, dissolve fully, stir often

say: At a 20 to 1 ratio, she needs 16 litres of water, so the covers can move freely. She pre-wets them, dissolves the dye fully, and stirs often. Dye all matching items in one batch.

say: Dye powders can irritate lungs and cause allergies, so wear a dust mask when measuring. Soda ash irritates skin and eyes, so wear gloves. Keep every dyeing cup and bucket for dyeing only, never for food.

cards.d: Dust mask when measuring powder, gloves for soda ash. Utensils for dyeing only, never food.
16 litres weighs about 16 kg. Fill it where you use it, lift with bent knees, keep hot baths from children.
Never into streams, gutters, near wells or boreholes, or onto vegetable gardens.

say: Test every batch. Wash a swatch for 30 minutes with a small piece of white cotton. Then rub a dry, then a damp, white cloth on the surface about 10 times. Colour on the white cloth means loose dye.

panel.heading: Aisha saves a failed batch
items: Wash test: 30 minutes with white cotton
Rub test: dry, then damp, about 10 times
Fail: rewash and retest
Pass: care label and batch number

say: For example, Aisha in Kano dyes 10 indigo napkins, and the damp cloth turns light blue. She soaks them, washes them hot twice, and tests again.

panel.heading: Aisha saves a failed batch
items: Wash test: 30 minutes with white cotton
Rub test: dry, then damp, about 10 times
Fail: rewash and retest
Pass: care label and batch number

say: Now there is only a faint tint. She writes wash separately for the first few washes on the care card, instead of rushing the batch out.

say: To remember. Use cotton-type fabric. Soda ash and 24 warm hours fix the colour. Rinse cold before untying. Work by dry weight for even colour. And test every batch, then write a care label in words, not only symbols.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Fibre-reactive dye: cotton, not polyester
Soda ash plus 24 warm hours fix colour
Rinse cold before untying
Work by dry weight: dye % and 20:1 water
Wash and rub test before every sale
